relationships.subject: RIN1
relationships.evidence_quote: Of importance was that genetic knockout of RIN1 from SOM+ interneurons blunted the replacement of GluN2B by GluN2A receptors during development, suggesting an important role of postsynaptic RIN1 in driving the GluN2B-to-GluN2A switch.

relationships.subject: Spinal SOM+ neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: suggesting that the SOM+ subpopulation served as the key component in the spinal circuits that relayed the mechanosensory information from the periphery to the ascending pain pathways

key_findings: RIN1 binds GluN2A and drives the GluN2B-to-GluN2A switch at primary afferent synapses on spinal SOM+ neurons during development and late neuropathic pain.
The switch alters analgesic efficacy of ifenprodil versus TCN-201 across SNI stages.
